title: Finite bases pass to completed constant quotient sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A\to B$ a homomorphism of commutative rings, and $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ an $A$-basis of $B$, with $d\geq0$. Let $t\in A$, $v\in B$, $u\in B^\times$ and $e\geq1$ satisfy $t=u v^e$ in $B$. Write $\underline{M}$ for the constant sheaf associated to an abelian group or ring $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $R=\lim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/t^nA}$ and $S=\lim_{m\geq1}\underline{B/v^mB}$. There is a unique ring map $R\to S$ whose $m$-th projection is $R\to\underline{A/t^mA}\to\underline{B/v^mB}$. Inverse limits are sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. The basis maps on the quotients induce an $R$-linear isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}S$, with $i$-th column the compatible residues of $b_i$. For every $n\geq1$, its projection at $m=en$ is the composite $R^{\oplus d}\to\underline{A/t^nA}^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{B/t^nB}=\underline{B/v^{en}B}$, where the first map is coordinatewise projection and the second is the quotient basis isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59: inverse limits of constant quotient sheaves. The basis and cofinal-filtration refinement below is an agent argument, not a numbered assertion of the source.

proof.text: Base change the given basis along A → A/t^(n+1). The tensor-product quotient equivalence identifies B ⊗_A A/t^(n+1) with B/(t^(n+1)B), carrying each base-changed basis vector to its residue. Since t maps to a unit times v^e, the extended ideal (t^(n+1))B equals (v^(e(n+1))). This gives the prescribed quotient basis, including d = 0.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-constant-specified-basis] to the quotient basis of step 1, with the explicit quotient algebra map. It gives the required isomorphism beta_n and exactly the specified finite-sum formula on sections.

proof.text: In $B$ one has $t^n=u^n v^{en}$, and multiplication by the unit $u^n$ gives $t^nB=v^{en}B$. Also $t^mB\subseteq v^mB$, since $em\geq m$. Hence $A\to B$ induces compatible ring maps $f_m:A/t^mA\to B/v^mB$: both composites from level $m+1$ send the class of $a$ to its image in $B/v^mB$. Use [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] to sheafify these maps. For $r=(r_n)\in R(U)$ set $f(r)_m=\underline f_m(U)(r_m)$. The transition equality makes this a compatible family; [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] identifies it with a section of $S(U)$. Componentwise it preserves the ring operations and restrictions. This constructs the required ring-sheaf map $f:R\to S$, and every map with the prescribed projections has exactly these coordinates, proving uniqueness.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: For each section of S and each n, use beta_n inverse to obtain its finite tuple of coordinates at level e(n+1)-1. The quotient finite-sum maps commute with reduction: the scalar maps commute by the quotient-map formulas, and constant basis columns commute by the sheafification unit. Their injectivity therefore makes the tuples compatible under A-quotient transitions.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: Define the completed linear map directly as the finite sum of coordinate projections followed by multiplication by the completed constant sections b_i. Evaluation preserves finite sums. Its cofinal projection is beta_n applied to the projected coordinates, using the compatibility of the completed scalar map with the cofinal scalar maps. Injectivity follows from the quotient basis maps and uniqueness in the sectionwise A-limit. For surjectivity, the compatible tuple from step 4 gives, for each i, a cone of sets; the preserved limit of ring sheaves supplies a completed coefficient. The finite product of these coefficients maps to the original section because cofinal projections determine a section of S. This is valid also for d = 0.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59, inverse-limit coefficient construction; elementary basis/cofinal-filtration refinement written by NS.

proof.text: The constructed map is already a morphism of module sheaves, by the unit-module/global-section equivalence. Its componentwise bijectivity makes the underlying additive presheaf map an isomorphism. Forgetful functors reflect isomorphisms, giving the required module-sheaf isomorphism. The same-level and cofinal projection formulas follow by applying ring projections to the finite sum and using their compatibility with the completed constants and scalar map. No separate cofinal-limit isomorphism is needed.
